rss.note: Mixed publication (CTF, pentest labs, bug bounty) — gated through the bug-bounty relevance filter, not trusted outright.

rss.name: Intigriti Blog
rss.note: Also publishes business/interview/news posts — gated through the relevance filter to keep only actual vulnerability writeups.

rss.name: r/netsec
rss.note: Broad subreddit — pre-filtered by keyword, then gated again through the relevance filter.

rss.name: Medium — #bug-bounty
rss.note: Medium's own tag feed — site-wide, not limited to one publication.

rss.name: Medium — #bugbounty
rss.note: Same as medium-tag-bug-bounty but the no-hyphen tag variant — some authors only use one.

rss.name: zseano
rss.note: Well-known individual bug bounty hunter's personal Medium blog.

rss.name: Assetnote
rss.note: Research team blog, heavy on real bounty-program findings — gated same as everyone else.

rss.name: PortSwigger Research
rss.note: Independent web security research, not bug-bounty-program writeups — off by default per user request to keep the feed bug-bounty-only. Flip enabled:true to bring it back.

rss.name: Zero Day Initiative
rss.note: Vendor CVE advisories (ZDI's own acquisition program), not bug bounty writeups — off by default, was the biggest source of noise in the first seed.

rss.name: RCE Security
rss.note: Independent CVE research, rarely tied to a bounty program — off by default.
